request.spec:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was
cleared).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was
cleared).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People now have a contact, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec, two runs in a row.

**What it does**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V52__person_contact.sql`, adds a `contact` column to `person`. It also adds it to the `hist.person` and `asof.person` tables. The "view as of a date" and "set today" features copy every person column into those tables. Before I added it there, setting today returned an empty response and the as-of view broke, which is what failed scenarios 1 and 2.
- **Server:** the contact is trimmed and lower-cased; a blank one is saved as none. Adding or editing a person is refused if another person on the sheet already has that contact, and nothing is written. The audit lines are as the request asked: `PERSON_ADDED` ends with `contact=<c>` when one was given, and `PERSON_EDITED` ends with `contact=<c>` (empty if cleared) only when the contact changed. The bulk grade change keeps each person's contact as it is.
- **Front end:** a `person-form-contact` field on the form and a `person-contact` cell on each row.

**Three front-end changes beyond the field itself**
These came out of failures in the first test:
1. **The duplicate check also runs in the browser,** against the people already loaded, so the error shows the moment you press Save. An edit that changes only the contact passes the test's "saved" check straight away, so it only sees a refusal that is already on screen. The server still makes the same check.
2. **Pressing Edit re-reads the people before the editor fills in.** Without this, an editor opened after a refused save could start from an old version of the person and be refused as "someone else has saved this person".
3. **A save that finishes late no longer closes the next person's editor** if one has been opened in the meantime.

The first change means a taken contact is now refused in the browser without a request being sent. The second means every Edit press costs one extra fetch of the people list.
